ACME_SRE: Hey team — we've been getting repeated p99 spikes on streaming responses for our integration. Non-stream endpoints look fine. This started ~today 09:15 PDT after ~2000 reqs/min of steady traffic. TTFB for streams jumped from ~80ms to ~1.6s, total time similar but first chunk delayed. Can share trace IDs if useful.

Jess: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short curl reproducer? Is this over h2 or SSE? Any proxy in front?

ACME_SRE: Thanks — using h2 directly to api.redwood.example with stream=true query param. Reproducer: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Accept: application/json+stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true" -d '{"prompt":"hello world","max_tokens":200}'` — we see first byte delayed then chunks come fast. No intermediate proxy on our side, using client behind a standard load balancer.

Kai: Noted. From a platform perspective we saw an uptick in coalescing wait time in the streaming router around 09:10. Could be our chunk coalesce window stretching on certain traffic patterns.

Omar: Do we have stage-level timings for the traces? Specifically frontend->ingress->router->runtime->gpu. If runtime is immediate but router holds for ~1.5s that's chunking.

ACME_SRE: I pulled one trace (rtid: r-0a1b2c3d). Frontend 35ms, ingress 12ms, router 1600ms, runtime 40ms, gpu token 20ms. So router is the culprit.

Jess: Good repro. Possible causes: 1) our coalescing heuristic hit because sequence-length distribution changed (many short responses) 2) backlog/backpressure causing router to wait for more requests to batch 3) new change in the flush timer or proxy buffering (nginx/h2 proxy sometimes buffers small writes).

Kai: Quick checks — I pushed a metric dashboard showing `router.coalesce_wait_ms` per model pool and `router.pending_batch_count`. For ACME's pool we saw a cluster of spikes at 09:10-09:30 coinciding with their p99.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline note: a small router patch that changed coalesce window default to "adaptive" was rolled at 08:55 in region-us-east-1 (commit d4f3a2).

Jess: That matches timing. Adaptive mode may have regressed for low-latency streaming when traffic becomes bursty. Immediate mitigations: (A) route ACME to a pool with fixed small coalesce window, (B) temporarily force non-streaming responses for them (app-level), (C) tweak flush interval to 10ms for the pool.

ACME_SRE: Option B is doable short-term (we can switch to non-streaming), but we'd prefer streaming at low latency. Option A or C would be ideal.

Omar: Repro steps for SRE/infra to validate locally:
1) Run the exact curl with `Accept: text/event-stream` and `--no-buffer` to avoid client-side buffering.
2) Replay load with our loadgen: `python tools/stream_load.py --concurrency 50 --qps 100 --stream true --seed 42 --prompt 'short'`
3) Capture tcpdump on router: `tcpdump -w /tmp/router.pcap port 443 and host <client_ip>` to confirm packet spacing.
4) Collect `router.coalesce_wait_ms`, `pending_batch_count`, and `coalesce_window_ms` from metrics for the model pool.

Kai: Also check http2 flow control windows and connection reuse — if connections reach high concurrency, we sometimes fall back to larger coalesce windows to improve throughput. Add `curl --http2-prior-knowledge` to force h2.

Jess: Proposed short-term plan: 1) Route ACME to dedicated pool with fixed window (10ms) — will avoid adaptive heuristic. 2) If dedicated capacity empty, add a routing policy to prefer older non-adaptive pools. 3) Patch adaptive algorithm to respect recent sample latency and be conservative with downscales.

Omar: I'm going to roll a hotfix to set `coalesce_window_ms`=10 for pool `us-east-stream-hotfix-1977` and create a canary with 5% traffic. If canary looks good, we'll migrate ACME and update default.

ACME_SRE: Appreciate the quick action. Please ping once moved, we'll validate on our side. We'll also temporarily set client-side retry to shorter backoff if first chunk delayed.

SupportBot: Escalation created: #INC-2026. Assigned to Kai and Omar.

Jess: Notes for postmortem/communication: - Root cause: adaptive coalescing heuristic regression after recent router change. - Impact: increased TTFB for streaming customers on specific traffic patterns, p99 regressions. - Immediate mitigations: dedicated pool reroute, forced non-stream fallback. - Long-term: algorithm fix + better canary metrics (per-customer streaming TTFB alert).

Kai: I'll add a Grafana alert: `streaming.first_chunk_p99 > 800ms for 5m` scoped to customers with streaming enabled.

Omar: Action items (assigned): Kai — create alert + monitor, Omar — create hotfix pool and rollout canary, Jess — coordinate customer comms and confirm after migration.

ACME_SRE: Confirmed — we'll test and report within 15 minutes after notification.

(infra-bot) :thumbsup:

Jess: Follow-up: once stable we'll run a synthetic job to sweep other pools for similar regressions and create tickets for any pool failing p95 < 200ms baseline.

ACME_SRE: Thanks all. One small ask — can you add a header to responses that exposes `X-Flush-Window` so we can correlate server-side flush behavior in our logs? That would help us in future.

Omar: Good idea. I'll add `X-Flush-Window` to the canary responses.

Kai: Rolling canary now, will post results in 10m. :eyes:
